item.title: The Nepal floods seem a world away – but make no mistake, climate breakdown will affect us all | Nesrine Malik
item.description: Richer countries might have more resources to deal with catastrophe, but this problem grips the entire planet, however much leaders may want to deny it Climate breakdown is happening on one Earth, but two different worlds. In one, its impacts increasingly encroach on everyday life; longer periods of discomfort and shorter periods of sharp pain. Endless, hotter summers, and within them sudden wildfires, evacuations, homes burned to cinders in a matter of hours. In another, catastrophe. This summer has been a snapshot of that split-screen. item.title: Nano-antennas make living cells light up brighter and faster
item.description: Researchers at Delft University of Technology have demonstrated for the first time that nano-antennas can enhance the fluorescence of proteins in living human and other mammalian cells. Scientists already use smart fluorescent proteins that light up when the electrical voltage across a nerve cell changes. By placing nano-antennas close to these light-emitting proteins, researchers can monitor processes inside cells with much greater precision. The discovery adds a new tool for revealing electrical signals in the brain through nanotechnology as well as genetic engineering. The research has… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chimpanzees have been hurling rocks at the same trees for more than a decade
item.description: Some chimpanzees in West Africa repeatedly throw rocks at particular trees, creating piles of stones that can remain in use for more than a decade. Researchers think this unusual behavior may be cultural and could serve as a form of communication, territorial signaling, or something more symbolic. Camera traps and audio recordings are now being used to reveal who throws the stones and how nearby chimpanzees respond. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Marruecos está levantando una infraestructura contra su gran enemigo. El plan: que todo el país esté conectado
item.description: Marruecos acaba de salir de una sequía que se prolongó durante siete años , pero en lugar de confiar en que las lluvias hayan resuelto el problema ha decidido acelerar una transformación completa de su sistema hídrico.
